correctness.rationale: The Frobenius factorization gives a pointwise quadratic-character identity over all finite extensions, including zeros and infinity. The derivative h'=c-x yields the complete discriminant and every root-multiplicity case; local equations give all delta invariants. A cubic Weierstrass model verifies the elliptic Hasse criterion. At nodal boundary parameters, the normalization conic and two Frobenius-exchanged/split preimages yield the stated zeta numerator. Exhaustive field tests (orders 3,9,27) and partial order81 pass, supplementing the symbolic argument.

originality.rationale: The 2022 Kudo–Nakagawa–Takagi article introduces the family, Cartier calculations, and smooth superspecial genus-four classification. It restricts its full automorphism appendix to p≥7 and analyzes p≡1,2 mod 3, so its statements do not imply the characteristic-three singular genus drop, exact rational/elliptic strata, or all-special-fiber zeta functions. Results for this family in characteristics five and seven have different geometric fibers and do not cover the asserted bad reduction. Published records searched did not provide the full theorem. Priority remains conditional on unindexed literature; a failed search alone is not proof of novelty.
residual_risks: Unindexed/older literature could describe the same special fiber or its zeta function under a different normalization.
The proof uses classical elliptic Hasse invariants, which alone must not be credited as a new result.

value.rationale: The known two-parameter smooth genus-four cyclic-cover family has an across-the-board characteristic-three genus-collapse with two intersecting exceptional coefficient divisors. The theorem classifies every resulting geometric normalization, singularity, elliptic supersingular subfamily, coefficient frequency, and singular zeta factor, including the reducible fiber. The exact arithmetic is a natural invariant for understanding bad reduction and would not follow from a random finite-point enumeration.
